name: Fury's Island County Park (Nobles County)
note: Nobles County park on a wooded peninsula between the Graham Lakes about a mile south of Maka-Oicu County Park, with lake access, a dock, a picnic shelter and a playground. The county posts no site count, site map or length, so pad size and whether any site has electric are unconfirmed. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Nobles County parks page (read 2026-11-12): 'Fury's Island County Park provides for camping, natural areas, lake access, showers, a large picnic shelter ... playground', 10 developed acres, 1 mile south of Maka-Oicu; county Park Rules & Fees page (read 2026-11-12): electric sites $25 / non-electric $15 a night, 'No reservations are taken for camper lots, these are on the first come basis'; Esri imagery 2025-10-02 (Vantor 0.31 m, rendered at ~1 km, ~470 m and z19) shows a gravel loop with spurs west of the shelter holding travel trailers/motorhomes of roughly 30 ft (e.g. 43.79133,-95.49395 and 43.79139,-95.49348), and the 2019-04-23 leaf-off Wayback frame (rendered) shows the same gravel spurs -> a real drive-in county campground with camper lots sold by the night (public: no price gate).
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-12: Esri World Imagery 2025-10-02 (Vantor WV03 0.31 m; export at ~1 km and ~470 m, z19 3x3 stitches over the south and east sides, all rendered) plus Esri Wayback leaf-off 2019-04-23 WV03 and 2011-04-28 UC-G (z18, rendered). The camper spurs sit in the peninsula's wooded interior: the west-loop units (43.79133,-95.49395; 43.79143,-95.49419) are ~45-50 m from the south shore behind a continuous 30-50 m wooded belt; the unit nearest the open lawn (43.79139,-95.49348) is ~49 m from the shore due south through dense trees and ~50 m from the open shoreline only via a tree clump and the day-use lawn, shore walk and dock (43.79104,-95.49293); the east and NE units (~43.79205,-95.4927; ~43.79258,-95.49307) are 65-75 m from the east shore through continuous canopy. No site map exists to place a named site on open ground at the water, and no source shows a sightline from a site -> not waterfront (same call as neighbouring 13332 Maka-Oicu, p3-439). Natural lakes, no dam.

fees.note: County-wide rate sheet: non-electric $15, electric $25 a night; 7 nights $150, 14 nights $300, a month $450, the season (May 1 - Labor Day weekend) $950. All campsite rates are halved after Labor Day weekend. Whether this park has electric sites is not stated.

flags: Site count and electric unconfirmed: Campendium (which the search snippets credit with 23 gravel sites, dry camping) refused with a Cloudflare 403 and was not read or retried. The county page says only 'camping' here, while it says Maka-Oicu campers 'have access to electricity'. The fee range 15-25 is the county-wide sheet, so the low figure may be the only one that applies; hookups and sites left absent.

Seasonal sites are sold (May 1 - Labor Day, $950) beside nightly FCFS camper lots; the 2025-10-02 frame shows about 5 units parked, the 2019-04-23 pre-season frame none. Nightly share not countable without a site count; a public county park with posted nightly rates, so kept.

Rig fit: the county gives no length; 2025 imagery shows units of roughly 30 ft on the gravel spurs (imagery, not a stated limit). Kept with the pad-size caveat (AWH 2026-11-02). No agency statement about access.

Google Maps (gm.py, 2026-11-12): 'Fury Island Park' at 43.79195,-95.49318, 3.0 stars from 1 review, no phone listed. Hipcamp's listing is an unclaimed scraped stub ('1 site', 'Coming soon') and was not used. AllStays detail pages returned decoy content (555 phone numbers, unrelated figures) and were not used. Nominatim refused (403) and was not retried, so the lakes are named only as the county names them ('East and West Graham Lakes').
Phone: the county Parks Office (507-468-2224), the same number 13332 Maka-Oicu carries; the parks supervisor's cell is also posted but not stored.
Duplicate check: nearest entry 13332 Maka-Oicu County Park 1.8 km N (a different park); nothing else within 8 km.
